prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored tokens loaded from persistent storage never get `token_expiry_time` recomputed, so `is_token_valid()`/proactive-refresh logic treats an actually-expired token as valid after a restart, ultimately forcing an interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored tokens loaded from persistent storage never get `token_expiry_time` recomputed, so `is_token_valid()`/proactive-refresh logic treats an actually-expired token as valid after a restart, ultimately forcing an interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause directly and minimally: it calls context.update_token_expiry() in _initialize() as soon as stored tokens with an expires_in are loaded, and ships a targeted test (expired_tokens fixture) for that exact code path. #2875's own inline comment describes this same missing-expiry-restoration bug as the reason its change is needed, but instead of restoring the expiry field it adds a new fallback branch ('Step 3.5') in async_auth_flow that tries a stored refresh_token before falling through to full re-authorization — a larger, more invasive change to the 401-retry control flow that treats the symptom rather than the underlying state bug, leaving any other code path that reads current_tokens.expires_in/token_expiry_time still working with stale data.

prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in pre_parse_json: for parameters whose annotation is a union that includes `str` (e.g. `str | None`), the function unconditionally tries `json.loads()` on incoming string values, silently corrupting legitimate strings that happen to parse as JSON (e.g. "null", "123", '{"a":1}') into the wrong type instead of leaving them as strings. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in pre_parse_json: for parameters whose annotation is a union that includes `str` (e.g. `str | None`), the function unconditionally tries `json.loads()` on incoming string values, silently corrupting legitimate strings that happen to parse as JSON (e.g. "null", "123", '{"a":1}') into the wrong type instead of leaving them as strings. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2032's _should_pre_parse_json generalizes the fix to any union composed entirely of simple scalar types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) via a reusable _SIMPLE_TYPES set, so it already covers the exact str | None case 3056 targets, plus additional cases like str | int | None that 3056 does not touch. 3056 is scoped narrowly to Optional[str] but adds one thing 2032 lacks: it unwraps Annotated[...] before the type check, so a field like `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is still correctly skipped — under 2032's plain membership check against _SIMPLE_TYPES, an Annotated-wrapped member would not match and pre-parsing would still incorrectly run. Recommend keeping 2032 as the base and folding in 3056's _unwrap_annotated step to close that gap.

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client permanently fails after MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the caller was never notified — the pending request just hung/failed silently instead of surfacing a clear error. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client permanently fails after MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the caller was never notified — the pending request just hung/failed silently instead of surfacing a clear error. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 is the more surgical fix: it constructs a JSONRPCError matching the outstanding request's id and delivers it through the same read_stream_writer the caller is already awaiting, and it explicitly gates this on `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which have no id to reply to) aren't mishandled — only the failed request is affected, other in-flight requests on the same session are untouched. #3098's approach instead raises a StreamableHTTPError to propagate up through the anyio TaskGroup (requiring a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig it back out of the resulting ExceptionGroup); under anyio TaskGroup semantics an exception in one task cancels all sibling tasks, so this would tear down the entire session/connection over a single stream's reconnection exhaustion rather than just failing the one affected request. #3098 also bundles in an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`) that widens the diff beyond the stated fix and isn't explained by the PR's stated purpose.

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: The read/write memory object streams in stdio_server() are created with a hardcoded buffer size of 0 (synchronous rendezvous channel), which can block a handler that needs to enqueue a second message (e.g. a final response right after a progress notification) while the previous write is still being flushed to stdout. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: The read/write memory object streams in stdio_server() are created with a hardcoded buffer size of 0 (synchronous rendezvous channel), which can block a handler that needs to enqueue a second message (e.g. a final response right after a progress notification) while the previous write is still being flushed to stdout. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2654 fixes the bug in the default path (write_stream buffer bumped 0->1) with no API changes required, and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the actual deadlock scenario from a progress notification followed by a response. 2215 only adds opt-in read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters defaulting to 0, so it does not change default behavior and would not fix the deadlock unless every caller remembers to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1. 2215's diff is also against a pre-refactor version of stdio.py (anyio.create_memory_object_stream) while 2654 and 2552 are based on the current create_context_streams helper, so 2215 is stale and would need a rebase/rework to even apply, with real merge-conflict risk against 2654's change to the same line.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 is the more surgical fix: it constructs a JSONRPCError matching the outstanding request's id and delivers it through the same read_stream_writer the caller is already awaiting, and it explicitly gates this on `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which have no id to reply to) aren't mishandled — only the failed request is affected, other in-flight requests on the same session are untouched. #3098's approach instead raises a StreamableHTTPError to propagate up through the anyio TaskGroup (requiring a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig it back out of the resulting ExceptionGroup); under anyio TaskGroup semantics an exception in one task cancels all sibling tasks, so this would tear down the entire session/connection over a single stream's reconnection exhaustion rather than just failing the one affected request. #3098 also bundles in an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`) that widens the diff beyond the stated fix and isn't explained by the PR's stated purpose.

clusters.pick_reason: 2032's _should_pre_parse_json generalizes the fix to any union composed entirely of simple scalar types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) via a reusable _SIMPLE_TYPES set, so it already covers the exact str | None case 3056 targets, plus additional cases like str | int | None that 3056 does not touch. 3056 is scoped narrowly to Optional[str] but adds one thing 2032 lacks: it unwraps Annotated[...] before the type check, so a field like `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is still correctly skipped — under 2032's plain membership check against _SIMPLE_TYPES, an Annotated-wrapped member would not match and pre-parsing would still incorrectly run. Recommend keeping 2032 as the base and folding in 3056's _unwrap_annotated step to close that gap.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 is the more surgical fix: it constructs a JSONRPCError matching the outstanding request's id and delivers it through the same read_stream_writer the caller is already awaiting, and it explicitly gates this on `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which have no id to reply to) aren't mishandled — only the failed request is affected, other in-flight requests on the same session are untouched. #3098's approach instead raises a StreamableHTTPError to propagate up through the anyio TaskGroup (requiring a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig it back out of the resulting ExceptionGroup); under anyio TaskGroup semantics an exception in one task cancels all sibling tasks, so this would tear down the entire session/connection over a single stream's reconnection exhaustion rather than just failing the one affected request. #3098 also bundles in an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`) that widens the diff beyond the stated fix and isn't explained by the PR's stated purpose.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs implement the same quote-aware comma-splitting tokenizer for WWW-Authenticate parsing (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041). #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which isolates the Bearer scheme's segment before parsing params. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead takes everything after the first space as the param list regardless of scheme, so it would misparse headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer error="x", DPoP nonce="y"') by pulling the second scheme's tokens into Bearer's param set. #3041 covers that additional case that #3012 does not.
